title: Intune adds maintenance windows for Windows updates
summary: Microsoft announced on 23 November 2026 that Windows update maintenance windows can now be configured in Intune (Devices > Manage devices > Maintenance windows), not only through Group Policy; a policy limits when automatic download, install and restart actions start for quality and feature updates, hotpatch, .NET, drivers and firmware. Windows can be one-time, daily, weekly or monthly (day 1–28 or week-based, such as the second Tuesday), 2–24 hours long in device-local time, and devices need Windows 11 24H2 with KB5077181 (build 26100.7840) or later. Actions started in a window can run past its end, and expedited updates, expired deadlines and grace periods, provisioning and minor-impact updates can still act outside it.
why: Kiosks and production or medical devices finally get Configuration Manager-style windows in cloud-only management. The catch is interaction: a deadline you set elsewhere can still force a restart outside the window, and a powered-off device that keeps missing its window stays unpatched.
todo: Use it only for userless and critical-use devices; regular users are better served by the normal update experience with deadlines.
Filter assignments to Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.7840 or later; older builds will not apply the setting.
Review deadlines, grace periods and expedited-update policies on the same devices before relying on the window.
Validate with update reports (install and restart times versus the window), not just policy deployment status.
effective_note: Available in Intune per Windows IT Pro Blog (23 Nov 2026) and Microsoft Learn.
